abstract: Census Bureau Business Formation Statistics for August 2026, released September 11, 2026. The universe-scale count of new US business applications and projected formations. AI's role is inferred from sectoral composition rather than tagged, so the series enters jobsdata.ai as context beneath the ai-business-formation chart rather than as a plotted value.
keyFindings: Business applications for August 2026, seasonally adjusted, were 531,728, a decrease of 7.8 percent from July 2026.
Projected business formations within four quarters were 28,501, down 4.6 percent from July.
The decline reverses July's 8.1 percent jump and returns applications close to their June 2026 level of about 531,000, so the July spike now reads as a one-month outlier rather than an inflection.
methodology: Derived from Employer Identification Number applications (IRS Form SS-4) covering the full universe of US business applications, with formations projected from historical transition rates between application and first payroll. Published monthly with national, regional, and state detail, seasonally adjusted.
qualifiers: Nothing in the series identifies AI as a driver: the AI reading comes from sectoral patterns, notably professional services growing faster than construction since ChatGPT, which is an inference rather than a measurement. Application counts are a weak proxy for real firm creation - many applications never become operating businesses, and the four-quarter formation projection is a model output, not an observation. Month-to-month moves of this size are common in the series and should not be over-read.
